summary: Replace the baseline with multi-start optimisation: random and ring-based initial centres, then SLSQP over (centres, radii) with a linear objective, pairwise non-overlap constraints and wall constraints. The best valid result is kept, and radii are shrunk slightly at the end to guarantee feasibility

Keep the multi-start phase, but spend most of the time on basin-hopping: perturb the best solution (Gaussian jitter, relocating the smallest circles, or swapping two circles of different radii), re-run SLSQP, and accept improvements. This should find much better packings than independent random star

Speed up SLSQP by constraining only nearby circle pairs (centre distance < 0.5), re-selecting the pairs in a second warm-started pass; this allows many more basin-hopping iterations in the same time. Radii are still repaired exactly by `_feasible_radii`, and the time budget is raised slightly.

I added a row-structured start (4–6 rows with random counts, evenly spaced and jittered) as a fourth start mode, so the multi-start phase begins from near-hexagonal layouts as well as random ones.
